merged.title: fix(port): the threads reading a track are stopped before the program exits
merged.author: ReaperOfVeriod
merged.untrustedBody:
## What

A music track is read and decoded on a thread of its own, and the thread was
detached: nothing waited for it. The player can close the window while a track
is being read, and the program then exits (`std::exit`) with that thread still
running. The static destructors take the mutex and the stream list away under
it, and the thread locks a mutex that no longer exists: a crash at quit, which
the crash handler catches and writes a report for. The launcher then says the
game stopped unexpectedly, when the player only closed it.

The readers are kept now, and the program stops them and waits for them before
it exits: in `leave()` (the window closed, the game ended) and through an
`atexit` handler for the other ways out (a run of so many frames, an error).
A reader that is already decoding finishes first, so nothing is taken away
under it.

merged.title: fix(port/rac1-pal): level copies run their own code
merged.author: Drustburn
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

Every level program of Ratchet & Clank (PAL) carries its own copy of much of
the engine, and a few level functions sit at several places of one program.
games/rac1's catalogue folds places of the same shape under one name. To run
those copies, the port registers each place under that name, picks a folded
call's target from the caller's own instructions, and relocates the
executable's addresses into the level loaded by pairing code. In the places
below this still made a level run a different function's code from the one
retail runs there, or relocate an address to the wrong place. This PR fixes
them in eight commits:

| | Commit | Touches |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | fix(port/rac1-pal): give the levels' copies of executable functions their own names | `split_places.tsv` rows; one host variant removed |
| 2 | fix(port/rac1-pal): the memory-card menu's states 23, 24 and 12 run their own steps in the levels | `split_places.tsv` rows |
| 3 | fix(port/rac1-pal): level 14's taxi and Play

merged.title: fix(hostgen): the matched C keeps the EE's integer widths
merged.author: Drustburn
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

hostgen reads the decompilation's C with Clang's integer widths, and the
PS2 has other ones. The compiler that built Ratchet & Clank's game code
(SN's GCC 2.95.3) has a 128-bit `long long`. The EE keeps a 32-bit value
sign-extended in its 64-bit register, and a register reaches the callee
with all its bits, whatever type the C gives it in between. Where the
matched C relies on that, the port moved 8 of 16 bytes in quadword
copies, and passed colours and texture words to 64-bit parameters with
another upper half than retail. This PR makes hostgen read those places
the EE's way, in seven commits:

| | Commit | Touches |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | fix(hostgen): a mode(TI) cast is 128 bits on any integer type | `prep.py` + test |
| 2 | fix(hostgen): long long is 128 bits in the game's own units | `prep.py`, `hostgen.py`, rac1-pal `hostgen.json` (`long_long_128`) + tests, README |
| 3 | fix(hostgen): a 32-bit value passed to a 64-bit parameter is sign-extended | `lower.py` + test |

merged.title: fix(hostgen): returns_64 results passed on whole; spilled 32-bit locals
merged.author: Drustburn
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

This follows #26 ("the matched C keeps the EE's integer widths"). #26
listed FastTweenColor (func_001FA8A8) in rac1-pal's `returns_64`: it
packs its colour with `ppach`/`ppacb` and leaves it zero-extended in
`$v0` (0x0000000080FFA888), and an int local that receives it keeps
all 64 bits, as the EE's register does. Three places of the matched C
still disagreed with the EE's registers about that colour:

- A function that only hands such a result back (`return
  FastTweenColor(...)` in an `int` function) was cut to 32 bits, so its
  callers sign-extended the colour again.
- An `unsigned int` local kept 64-bit for such a result that takes
  another 32-bit value on a second path got that value zero-extended
  by C's conversion, where `addu`, `lui`/`ori` or `lw` leave it
  sign-extended in the register.
- A local the original keeps in a stack slot across calls is stored
  with `sw` and loaded back with `lw`, so on the EE it holds the
  sign-extended low half, not the whole resul

merged.title: fix(launcher): the AppImage's own environment stays in the AppImage
merged.author: ReaperOfVeriod
merged.untrustedBody:
## What this changes

Two things about the Linux AppImage, both found by running the released
0.8.4 AppImage and by running the same build on a Steam Deck.

**The AppImage's environment.** AppImageKit's `AppRun` sets `PYTHONHOME`,
`PYTHONPATH`, `PERLLIB`, `GST_PLUGIN_SYSTEM_PATH`, `QT_PLUGIN_PATH` and
`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` before the launcher starts, all pointing into the
AppImage. This AppImage carries no Perl, no GStreamer and no Qt, so
those variables point at nothing — a Qt program told to look for its
platform plugin in ten directories that do not exist says "Could not find
the Qt platform plugin" and stops. The launcher now takes them back
(`core/src/appimage.rs`): the ones that mean nothing go, and everything
the launcher starts (the game, the tools, and the program that opens a
link or a folder) gets the system's own environment. The launcher's own
webview keeps the AppImage's libraries, since `WebKitWebProcess` finds
the AppImage's WebKit nowhere else.

merged.title: feat: extract and build every level from both discs, recount functions from the binaries
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
Levels pulled out of the discs properly, every program built byte-identical, and the functions recounted from the binaries. No matching in here, just restructure.

**Both discs**
- `tools/levels.py dump` reads the main program and all 49 programs (main image, frontbin, 47 levels) straight from the ISO's table of contents. No wrench unpack needed.
- `tools/build_levels.py` rebuilds every program from its assembly and checks it against the disc: 49/49 MATCH on US (SCUS_974.65) and on PAL (SCES_532.85).
- US is the primary target; PAL is the second version. Tools take `--version us|pal`, tables live in `config/us/` and `config/pal/`.

**Counting (rac1-decomp's rules)**
- Starts, joined pieces, padding and linker remnants found from the binaries; each distinct function counted once (copy levels, frontbin's second link of the menu code, k-th copy rule).
- US: 15,056 functions / 5,175,440 bytes before, 18,085 / 5,782,424 now. The old list left 452 KB of the menu `.text` uncut and counted lev

merged.title: Add PAL versions of 16 functions whose US C differs on PAL (src/pal/)
merged.author: chistianh
merged.untrustedBody:
These are `differs` rows of config/pal/map.tsv listed in docs/levels.md: the US C in src/ builds only to the US bytes. Each file here is the US C with the constants that table lists changed to the PAL values (50 Hz timings, 25/30 frame counts, a float 50.0 against 60.0, animation ids), named after the PAL function. Every one gives MATCH with
`tools/check_func.py --version pal NAME file.c` on SCES_532.85 (checked with the final files), and a deliberately wrong constant gives BYTES.

Not done here, because tools/match_map.py and tools/progress.py need the US dumps (baserom/us/main.elf), which this contributor does not have: config/us/map.tsv, config/pal/map.tsv and the two progress reports still need regenerating.

merged.title: Add PAL C for the remaining 16 `differs` functions; use PAL callee names in src/pal/
merged.author: chistianh
merged.untrustedBody:
This finishes the docs/levels.md table of US functions that differ on PAL: with these 16 every row has PAL C in `src/pal/`.

**7 functions whose PAL twin differs only by constants or global offsets**
func_004F6660, func_L00_00599F58, func_L00_006BB798, func_L00_007158A0, func_L00_00718458, func_L01_0055B6A8, func_L41_003DFDA0. These are 50 Hz timings (×5/6), shifted globals and one hardcoded address. Globals are named after the PAL address their instructions reach: HI16/LO16 pairs, and `$gp` = 0x2259FF for GPREL16.

**9 functions that changed for PAL (no PAL twin of the US code)**
Each PAL function was found between the nearest US neighbours that `config/pal/map.tsv` places on PAL, then confirmed by the shape of its code (89–98% alike; the next candidate was far below).

| US | PAL | What changed on PAL |
|---|---|---|
| func_004A2698 | func_004A3388 | the menu has five entries (texts 0x153 and 0x154 added) |
| func_004AD3E0 | func_004AE260 | also sets +0x158 of the entry to -1 |
| fun
